set.approach: No turn-by-turn approach is published. The north flank of Jack Mountain is reached from the Ross Lake East Bank Trail, which begins at the East Bank Trailhead on SR 20 near milepost 138 (~1,800 ft); Ross Lake Resort's water taxi will also drop parties at points along the eastern shore, which shortens the trail walking considerably. Devils Creek is the main north-side drainage and the East Bank Trail crosses it. From wherever you leave the trail, expect a steep, brushy, cliff-banded climb through timber to reach open ground and the base of the ridge — on the Nohokomeen side, the same belt of terrain has cliff bands starting around 3,200 ft, threaded on game trails to reach snow near 4,800-5,000 ft. Treat the approach as exploratory: study current imagery and plan the line before committing.

set.descent_text: This is a walk-off/downclimb — no rappelling on the standard Southwest Ridge scramble route. From the summit, reverse the ridge scramble back down to the head of the scree slope, then descend the same loose scree/talus line back into the Star Lake basin. Stay on or near the ascent line: do not descend the boulder field on the east side of the peak, which is dangerous with unstable, car-sized talus. Loose rock and scree underfoot make the descent slow and slippery regardless of line, and if snow is still present on the upper slopes it typically softens through the day, so rock underneath can pull loose late — an earlier start/turnaround reduces this. From Star Lake, reverse the West Fork Buttermilk Creek Trail (#411): back up over Fish Creek Pass, down through the larch zone, through the blowdown-choked lower trail, and back across the West Fork Buttermilk Creek fords to the trailhead.
